s92-ep-021.text: In the S-92 Emergency Procedures, what does the term "land as soon as possible" mean? -- Correct: Land at the nearest site where a safe landing can be accomplished. The RFM defines "land as soon as possible" as landing at the nearest site where a safe landing can be accomplished. "Land immediately" means continued flight may not be possible and ditching or landing in hazardous terrain is preferable to continuing flight; "land as soon as practical" means extended flight is not recommended, with landing site and duration of flight at the pilot's discretion.
s92-ep-021.note: p.3-2 INTRODUCTION: definitions of land immediately / land as soon as possible / land as soon as practical read on the image; all three match the explanation. Distractor D is not an RFM definition. [DOC page 113 of the full RFM; checked on the page image rendered at 130 dpi]

s92-ep-022.text: According to the Emergency Procedures introduction, when should the pilot reset a popped circuit breaker? -- Correct: Only if the affected system is required for flight, only once, and only if there is no indication of electrical fire. A circuit breaker should be reset only if the affected system is required for flight. The pilot should reset a circuit breaker only once and only if there is no indication of electrical fire.
s92-ep-022.note: p.3-2 INTRODUCTION, last NOTE: reset only if the affected system is required for flight; only once; only if no indication of electrical fire. Confirmed on the image. [DOC page 113 of the full RFM; checked on the page image rendered at 130 dpi]

s92-ep-023.text: After an emergency engine shutdown (throttle STOP, FUEL OFF), TGT remains above 540°. What does the procedure call for? -- Correct: Press the ENG START button to engage the starter with the throttle in STOP, and press it again to turn the starter off when TGT is below 150°. If TGT remains above 540° or there is other evidence of combustion after engine shutdown, press the ENG START button to engage the starter with the throttle in STOP. When TGT is below 150°, press the ENG START button to turn the starter off.
s92-ep-023.note: p.3-3 1.1 EMERGENCY ENGINE SHUTDOWN: steps 1 Throttle STOP, 2 FUEL OFF; 'If TGT remains above 540 deg or there is other evidence of combustion' step 3 ENG START PRESS to engage starter with throttle in STOP; 'When TGT is below 150 deg' step 4 ENG START PRESS to turn starter off. Page prints degrees without C; kept as printed. [DOC page 114 of the full RFM; checked on the page image rendered at 130 dpi]

s92-ep-024.text: An engine flamed out while its fuel selector was in XFD. According to ENGINE RESTART IN FLIGHT, what should be done with the fuel selector for the restart? -- Correct: Place the fuel selector switch to DIRECT during the restart sequence. The ENGINE RESTART IN FLIGHT procedure assumes the engine was operating with the fuel selector in DIRECT. If the flameout occurred while operating in XFD, place the fuel selector switch to DIRECT during the restart sequence.
s92-ep-024.note: p.3-3 1.2 ENGINE RESTART IN FLIGHT NOTE: procedure assumes fuel selector in DIRECT; if flameout occurred in XFD, place fuel selector switch to DIRECT during restart sequence. Confirmed on image. [DOC page 114 of the full RFM; checked on the page image rendered at 130 dpi]

s92-ep-025.text: During an in-flight engine restart using crossbleed air, what does the CAUTION require on the operating engine? -- Correct: At least 90% Ng. The CAUTION states: maintain at least 90% Ng on the operating engine when accomplishing a crossbleed start. The same caution appears in both ENGINE RESTART IN FLIGHT and EMERGENCY ENGINE START.
s92-ep-025.note: p.3-4 CAUTION and p.3-5 CAUTION: 'Maintain at least 90% Ng on the operating engine when accomplishing a crossbleed start.' Confirmed on both images. The 80% torque figure (distractor A) belongs to the air-source note on p.3-4. [DOC page 115, 116 of the full RFM; checked on the page image rendered at 130 dpi]

s92-ep-026.text: During an in-flight engine restart with AIR SRCE HEAT/START in ENG and the APU on, which air source does the system use? -- Correct: The operating engine if it is at approximately 80% torque or above; otherwise the APU. With the AIR SRCE HEAT/START switch in ENG and the APU on, the system uses the engine as the air source if the operating engine is at approximately 80% torque or above; below approximately 80% torque it uses the APU. The APU should be ON for in-flight restarts if possible, and use of engine cross-bleed results in a loss of up to 3% power of the operating engine.
s92-ep-026.note: p.3-4 NOTE (change-barred): APU should be ON for in-flight restarts if possible; cross-bleed loses up to 3% power of operating engine; with AIR SRCE HEAT/START in ENG and APU on, engine is the air source at approx 80% torque or above, APU below approx 80%. Confirmed on image. [DOC page 115 of the full RFM; checked on the page image rendered at 130 dpi]

s92-ep-027.text: What protection is absent during the EMERGENCY ENGINE START procedure, and what must the pilot do about it? -- Correct: FADEC hot start prevention is not present; the pilot must monitor engine temperature and place the throttle to STOP if a hot start is imminent. During normal engine starts, hot start prevention is provided automatically by the FADEC. This protective feature is not present during an emergency start procedure: the pilot must monitor engine temperature and manually abort the start by placing the throttle to STOP if a hot start is imminent. An emergency start is only to be used when damage to the engine is secondary to safety of flight.
s92-ep-027.note: p.3-4 1.3 intro sentence (damage to engine secondary to safety of flight); p.3-5 first CAUTION: hot start prevention not present in emergency start; pilot monitors temperature and places throttle to STOP if hot start imminent. Confirmed on images. [DOC page 115, 116 of the full RFM; checked on the page image rendered at 130 dpi]

s92-ep-028.text: During the EMERGENCY ENGINE START procedure, when is the throttle of the affected engine moved to FLY? -- Correct: When TGT is below 150°C, or sooner if the situation dictates. The emergency start sequence is: APU CTRL ON (if time permits), AIR SRCE HEAT/START to ENG (if APU is OFF) or APU (if APU is ON), ENG IGN AUTO, FUEL selector DIRECT or XFD, throttle OFF, ENG START button PRESS, then throttle to FLY when TGT is below 150°C or sooner if the situation dictates. The emergency start procedure overrides the FADEC automatic blow down.
s92-ep-028.note: p.3-5 action steps 1-7 read on image: step 5 throttle OFF, step 6 ENG START PRESS, step 7 throttle FLY when TGT below 150 deg C or sooner if the situation dictates. p.3-4 NOTE: emergency start overrides automatic blow down. [DOC page 115, 116 of the full RFM; checked on the page image rendered at 130 dpi]

s92-ep-029.text: After a single engine failure, how is 30 second power re-armed? -- Correct: By pushing forward on the collective OEI SEL switch, at any time. Thirty second power can be re-armed at any time by pushing forward on the OEI SEL switch. After an engine failure, 30 second power is attained by raising the collective until Nr decreases to 100%. Moving the switch aft selects two minute power; pushing in on it (after two minute power is selected) selects maximum continuous power.
s92-ep-029.note: p.3-6 first paragraph: 30 second power attained by raising collective until Nr decreases to 100%; two minute power by moving OEI SEL aft; MCP by first selecting two minute then pushing in; 30 second power re-armed at any time by pushing forward on OEI SEL. Confirmed on image. [DOC page 117 of the full RFM; checked on the page image rendered at 130 dpi]

s92-ep-030.text: While cushioning a single engine landing, Nr droops below 96%. If the APU and APU generator are not on, what is the result? -- Correct: The AC generators drop off line, only the battery bus powers aircraft systems and the copilot MFDs momentarily blank, with no degradation to aircraft control. When increasing collective to cushion a single engine landing, Nr may droop below 96%, causing the AC generators to drop off line at touchdown. Unless the APU is on and the APU generator switch is on, only the battery bus will be available. This does not degrade aircraft control but causes the copilot MFDs to momentarily blank. Once the collective is moved to flat pitch and Nr recovers above 96%, normal electrical power returns.
s92-ep-030.note: p.3-6 first NOTE: Nr below 96% -> AC generators drop off line at touchdown; unless APU on and APU GEN on, only battery bus; no degradation to aircraft control; copilot MFDs momentarily blank; power returns with flat pitch and Nr above 96%. Confirmed on image. [DOC page 117 of the full RFM; checked on the page image rendered at 130 dpi]

s92-ep-031.text: Extended single engine flight is needed to reach a safe landing area. When does the RFM say NOT to use fuel crossfeed? -- Correct: When the pilot suspects the engine failed due to a fuel system malfunction. If extended single engine flight is required, the pilot should use the fuel crossfeed system to prevent exceeding 700 pounds (317 kg) of fuel imbalance or to prevent flaming out the good engine due to fuel starvation. Do not crossfeed if the pilot suspects that the engine failed due to a fuel system malfunction.
s92-ep-031.note: p.3-6 second NOTE: use crossfeed to prevent exceeding 700 lb (317 kg) imbalance or fuel starvation of the good engine; do not crossfeed if engine failure suspected due to fuel system malfunction. Confirmed on image. Distractor B inverts the note (crossfeed is used to prevent exceeding 700 lb). [DOC page 117 of the full RFM; checked on the page image rendered at 130 dpi]

s92-ep-032.text: An engine fails during a Category A horizontal takeoff exactly at the takeoff decision point (TDP). What does the RFM direct? -- Correct: Reject the takeoff. If the engine fails before or at the takeoff decision point (TDP), the takeoff is rejected. If the failure occurs after the TDP, the takeoff may be continued. Prior to reaching TDP, the rejected takeoff is initiated by rotating nose up to decrease forward speed and attain a landing attitude.
s92-ep-032.note: p.3-6 1.6 intro: fails before or at TDP -> takeoff rejected; after TDP may be continued. p.3-6A 'Prior to Reaching TDP' step 1 rotate nose up to decrease forward speed and attain landing attitude. Confirmed on images. [DOC page 117, 118 of the full RFM; checked on the page image rendered at 130 dpi]

s92-ep-033.text: Following an engine failure on a Category A takeoff, what rotor speed does the RFM specify from the TDP up to the best rate of climb speed, and for single engine flight above it? -- Correct: 100% Nr from TDP to Vy (80 KIAS), then 105% Nr for single engine flight above Vy. During a Category A climbout, 100% Nr is used to maximize climb rates from TDP to the best rate of climb speed of 80 KIAS. For single engine flight above the best rate of climb airspeed, use 105% Nr.
s92-ep-033.note: p.3-6 last paragraph: 100% Nr from TDP to best rate of climb speed of 80 KIAS; single engine flight above best rate of climb airspeed use 105% Nr. Confirmed on image. [DOC page 117 of the full RFM; checked on the page image rendered at 130 dpi]

s92-ep-034.text: After an engine failure past the TDP in a Category A horizontal takeoff, when should two minute power be selected? -- Correct: Not until obstacle clearance is assured; select it when obstacles are cleared. After TDP: adjust pitch attitude to establish Vtoss, adjust collective to maintain 100% Nr, and retract the landing gear when a positive rate of climb is established. A WARNING states: do not select two minute power until obstacle clearance is assured. When obstacles are cleared, select two minute power, continue the climb and accelerate to Vy, then select maximum continuous power and land as soon as practical.
s92-ep-034.note: p.3-7 After TDP steps 1-7 and WARNING read on image: Vtoss, 100% Nr, gear up at positive climb, WARNING no two minute power until obstacle clearance assured, step 4 select two minute power when obstacles cleared, 5 accelerate to Vy (5.1 RIPS HEAVY in icing), 6 MCP, 7 land as soon as practical. [DOC page 119 of the full RFM; checked on the page image rendered at 130 dpi]
